claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi forms a simple, single-phase FCC solid solution in the applicable starting state.
The equimolar CoCrFeNiTi FCC starting state has low hardness and strength together with high plasticity and machinability.
Low hardness and strength in equimolar FCC CoCrFeNiTi are governed by inherently high dislocation mobility.
Equimolar FCC CoCrFeNiTi has a high stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy promotes more active dislocation motion relative to mechanical twinning.
High stacking-fault energy reduces lattice resistance to dislocation glide.
High stacking-fault energy minimizes the formation of dislocation forests and entanglements.
Suppression of dislocation forests and entanglements limits strain hardening, hardness, and yield strength.
Easy dislocation glide accounts for the alloy's high ductility and machinability.
Temperature and strain rate are relevant variables for challenging the proposed dislocation-mobility mechanism.

The controlled comparison varies temperature between approximately 25°C and 0°C and varies strain rate within a low-to-moderate quasi-static regime while holding composition and FCC structural state fixed.
TEM and diffraction measurements can be combined with mechanical testing to assess dislocation arrangements, lattice strain, and microstructural evolution.
Across the proposed temperature and strain-rate range, CoCrFeNiTi should retain mobile dislocation configurations with little forest or entanglement formation.
Any dislocation pile-ups induced by the modified loading conditions should be transient, and steady-state strain hardening should remain low.
Decreasing temperature can normally increase yield strength in an equiatomic FCC high-entropy alloy.
Minor mechanical twinning may compete with dislocation glide under extreme conditions.

A pronounced increase in dislocation-forest formation, yield strength, and strain-hardening rate at higher strain rate or lower temperature would falsify the claim that high dislocation mobility alone governs the low strength.
